 Popular YouTuber arrested in Henderson on felony child sex crime charges from California 
 A revived California investigation led to Bryant Moreland’s arrest. 
 Well-known YouTube personality Bryant Moreland, widely recognized online as “EDP445,” was arrested this week in Henderson. By Victoria Saha and Martha Cruz Published : Nov. 5, 2026 at 5:05 PM PST | Updated : Nov. 5, 2026 at 5:12 PM PST Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google LAS VEGAS ( FOX5 ) — Well-known YouTube personality Bryant Moreland, widely recognized online as “EDP445,” was arrested this week in Henderson on four felony sex crime charges involving a minor stemming from a California case.
 Moreland was arrested on a warrant just before noon on Wednesday, November 4 near Green Valley and Pebble, according to the Henderson Police Department. He was later booked into the Clark County Detention Center where he remained on Thursday.
 2021 case did not result in charges
 Moreland did not face charges after the 2021 incident. The District Attorney’s Office said it reviewed the incident in 2021 and 2022 and faced significant challenges in pursuing prosecution, particularly because the reporting parties did not cooperate.
 The District Attorney’s Office and the Kern County Sheriff’s Office reopened the investigation after Moreland’s statements in the documentary. The District Attorney’s Office said that after reviewing the new evidence, it determined the evidentiary threshold for filing charges had been met.
 However, prosecutors said statements Moreland made in a 2026 documentary titled “The Sick Mind of EDP445” revived the case and ultimately led to his arrest in Southern Nevada.
 View this post on Instagram A post shared by FOX5 Las Vegas (@fox5vegas) 
 Documentary creator responds
 Mike Clum, the creator of the documentary, said most of it was filmed in Las Vegas, where Moreland lived.
 “I was surprised when the investigation was opened,” Clum said. “And I was reached out to by Kern County, obviously. My documentary footage, while the intent wasn’t to gather evidence, it ended up being evidence.”
 In footage featured in the documentary, Moreland addressed the allegations, at one point referencing his actions involving a 13-year-old and attributing them to “desperation.”
 Clum noted that Moreland’s demeanor varied throughout filming.
 “He processes what happened, he goes through phases,” Clum said. “There’s times he feels remorse... then he extroverts that and says that’s someone else’s fault. It depends on his mood.”
 The documentary shows Moreland with millions of followers on YouTube.
 Online Reaction and Arrest
 Moreland previously amassed millions of followers on YouTube before becoming one of the platform’s most notorious figures following the initial allegations.
 After criminal charges were filed this week, fellow content creator Jidion Adams, known online as “JiDion,” flew from Texas to Henderson to witness Moreland’s arrest in person.
 “This arrest was so important because he’s one of ours, sadly,” Adams said. “We all have been wanting this to happen for so long. It’s been an inside joke in our community of, like, he’s untouchable. He can’t get arrested.”
 Adams, who operates an investigative group called “EDP Watch,” stated that Moreland’s evasion of prosecution had long served as the catalyst for their broader tracking efforts.
 “The reason why we’re doing this is because EDP was the one that got away,” Adams said. “So to finally have that happen where he’s finally caught and arrested and finally facing the charges that he should have been facing five years ago... everybody collectively for one time on the internet all came together and said that this is one hell of a thing.”
 What happens next
 Moreland was taken to the Clark County Detention Center. Fox5 asked the jail for an interview with Moreland. The jail said interviews are not possible because of where he is located in the facility.
 There has been no confirmation of any charges against Moreland in Las Vegas.
 Moreland is expected to face a judge in Las Vegas Monday. The District Attorney’s Office said an arraignment hearing will be scheduled after Moreland is extradited to Kern County. 
 Kern County officials said they cannot release any other documents until he is arraigned.
 The District Attorney’s Office adds that a defendant is presumed innocent unless and until the charges are proven in court beyond a reasonable doubt.
